defects.summary: Persists the entered email and plaintext password together in localStorage when 'keep me signed in' is checked, and reads them back to prefill the login form; any script with page access (e.g. XSS) can read the raw password directly.
Renders the catalog item's description via Svelte's {@html} tag without sanitization; if the description ever contains attacker-controlled markup, arbitrary script executes in the viewer's session.

Restores the authenticated user from an unvalidated localStorage cache with no server-side session/token check; editing the cached value in devtools impersonates any user, since the app trusts client-stored state alone as proof of authentication.

Defines a payment-signing key as a VITE_-prefixed env var with a hardcoded fallback secret, both of which end up inlined into the client-side JavaScript bundle at build time; anyone can extract the signing key from the shipped code.
Sets a Content-Security-Policy with script-src allowing 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', and any https: origin; this combination defeats CSP's main XSS mitigation.

Uses $effect to derive actionLabel from calculation and to reset errorMessage as a side effect, instead of computing actionLabel with $derived; effects are meant for side effects, not for producing a value that could simply be a derived expression.

Destructures name/description/price/tags out of the item prop into plain consts; this snapshots the values at that point, so updates to item after the initial render are not reflected in the rendered fields.

Calls item.tags.sort() directly on a non-bindable prop, mutating the parent's array in place; child components should treat props as one-way data from the parent, and this mutation can silently affect the parent's state.

Makes the onMount callback async and returns a cleanup function from inside it; onMount only treats a synchronously returned function as a teardown callback, so the async callback's return value is a Promise, and the intended worker.stop() cleanup is silently never registered.

Registers the keydown listener inside onMount instead of $effect; Svelte 5's guidance is to use $effect for DOM-interfacing side effects since it composes with reactivity and unifies cleanup timing, rather than mixing onMount (mount-once) and $effect lifecycles for closely related DOM wiring.
Removes the typed Props interface and destructures $props() without a type annotation, making every prop implicitly any and losing all compile-time type checking for this component's public API.

Passes { keepFocus: true } to goto() on a full-page navigation after logout; this suppresses SvelteKit's default focus reset to <body>, leaving keyboard/screen-reader focus on an element from the page that no longer exists.

Passes { keepFocus: true } to goto() on a full-page navigation after a successful login; this suppresses SvelteKit's default focus reset to <body>, leaving keyboard/screen-reader focus on an element from the login page that no longer exists.

Passes { keepFocus: true } to goto() on a full-page navigation after a successful registration; this suppresses SvelteKit's default focus reset to <body>, leaving keyboard/screen-reader focus on an element from the registration page that no longer exists.

Destructures cart out of the appState class instance into a local const; this snapshots the reactive property's value once, so subsequent updates to appState.cart are not reflected in the destructured binding used for quantity display.

Changes the catalog state from $state.raw (shallow, reference-based reactivity) to plain $state, which deeply proxies every item in the array; since the catalog is only ever replaced wholesale from the API response, this adds proxy-wrapping overhead with no reactivity benefit.

Calls connectivity.subscribe() inside onMount but discards the returned unsubscribe function; the subscription is never torn down when the component unmounts, leaking a store subscription for the lifetime of the app.

Threads a hardcoded currency prop through the new CartItemList intermediate component purely to forward it to CartLineItem, without CartItemList itself using the value; this is prop drilling for a constant that could be a module-level constant or context instead.

Moves price formatting and tag-type classification out of ProductCard (a presentational concern belonging with the component rendering it) into the top-level route component, which now owns formatting/classification logic for every card instead of letting each card be self-contained -- a step toward a God Component absorbing unrelated responsibilities.
